name: GO Classes GATE CS/DA | DBMS | ER Model | Weekly Quiz 17

question.text:
A conference session will be attended by a number of delegates. Each delegate may choose a number of sessions. What is the relationship between conference delegates and sessions?

  1. One-to-One $(1: 1)$
     
  2. One-to-Many ( $1: M$ )
     
  3. Many-to-One ( $M: 1$ )
     
  4. Many-to-Many ( $M: N$ )

Following ER Diagram represents the commitments that teachers and students have during the semester. (The diagram is incomplete)

  • Students may lead multiple clubs, and every club has one student leader.
     
  • Students can also participate in multiple clubs, and every club has at least one student member.
     
  • Every teacher has multiple office hours, and one teacher leads each office hour.


Which of the following options is/are correct?

  1. We should draw a thick arrow (arrow pointing towards the leads relationship set) to connect the Clubs entity with the leads relationship set.
     
  2. We should draw a thick line to connect the Clubs entity with the participates relationship set.
     
  3. We should draw a thick line to connect the Teachers entity with the have relationship set.
     
  4. A class can be taught by multiple teachers.

The figure with ovals and circles below illustrates a relationship set between two entity sets. Each circle is an entity or relationship, and the edges connect them. The ER diagram right below that figure needs to be complete with constraints that are consistent with the edges in the diagram. For each of the following, match the statements with the correct constraint:
 

\[
\begin{array}{l@{\hspace{4cm}}l}
\textbf{Statements:} & \textbf{Constraints:} \\[2mm]

\text{a) A bold edge between E1 and R is:} &
\text{i) needed} \\[1mm]

\text{b) An arrowhead between E1 and R is:} &
\text{ii) optional} \\[1mm]

\text{c) A bold edge between E2 and R is:} &
\text{iii) disallowed} \\[1mm]

\text{d) An arrowhead between E2 and R is:} &
\end{array}
\]


$\textbf{Choose the correct combination:}$

  1. a-iii, b-iii, c-ii, d-ii
     
  2. a-i, b-iii, c-ii, d-ii
     
  3. a-iii, b-i, c-iii, d-i
     
  4. a-ii, b-ii, c-i, d-iii

Based on the ER diagram shown above, which of the following options is/are True?

  1. Each course has at least one student.
     
  2. Every student has taken at least one course.
     
  3. A student can take $3$ courses.
     
  4. A course can have $3$ students.

Which of the following is/are FALSE ?

  1. ER diagrams are used to model the physical schema of a database.
     
  2. An entity set $E$ can be associated with a relationship set $R$ more than once.
     
  3. At most $2$ distinct entity sets can be associated with any relationship set $R$.
     
  4. A weak entity set must have total participation in its identifying relationship set.

In Database Management Systems (DBMS), an Entity-Relationship (ER) model utilizes different types of attributes to represent entity properties. Consider an Employee entity with the following attributes:

  1. An attribute Full_Name that can be broken down into independent subcomponents: First_Name, Middle_Name, and Last_Name.
     
  2. An attribute Skill_Set where a single employee can possess multiple distinct values (e.g., Python, SQL, Java) simultaneously.
     
  3. An attribute Years_of_Service that is automatically calculated by subtracting the employee's Date_of_Join from the current calendar date.
